written_before: D_attack_dev was generated and long before D_final was opened

ATTACK_W.property: |delta_d| = eps exactly (Theorem S is tight here)
ATTACK_W.purpose: certificate validation -- this is the attack the geometry is stated against

ATTACK_V.purpose: behavioural robustness -- the attack that actually changes generation

grid_rule.why: Anchoring on one fixed scalar gives ABSOLUTE epsilon values identical for every rho, while the level set is chosen to satisfy section 40: zero, below the smallest family certificate (0.3, 0.6), between certificates (0.9), just below and just above the Cantor certificate (0.98, 1.02), and well above every certificate (1.5, 2.4, 3.6).

GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.decided_on: D_attack_dev, before the protocol freeze and before D_final was opened
GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.problem: The certificate scale and the behavioural scale are ~11x apart. epsilon_Cantor = 2W/27 = 0.1689 in residual L2 units is only 0.9% of ||h_P0|| ~ 18.4, whereas V3.3.5b/c established that behaviour only starts moving at a relative perturbation q ~ 0.10, i.e. ||delta_h|| ~ 1.84.
GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.evidence: On D_attack_dev the whole certificate-anchored grid (0 to 3.6 x epsilon_C = 0.608) moved the safe rate only 0.76 -> 0.68 for both attack families.
GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.consequence_if_not_extended: Section 43 asks whether a larger certified radius produces later BEHAVIOURAL failure. A grid that never reaches the behavioural threshold cannot answer that question in either direction.
GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.extension: Four levels were added, anchored on relative perturbation rather than on the certificate: 5.45x, 10.9x, 21.8x and 43.7x epsilon_C, which correspond to q = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20 and 0.40 at the median ||h_P0||.
GRID_EXTENSION_DISCLOSURE.outcome_independence: The added values are identical for every rho and were chosen from the residual-norm scale alone. No rho outcome was consulted.
